alex: Heads-up — after the FlashAttention kernel swap on canary we saw a 10-14% drop in delivered throughput for 13B-ish workloads. Looks like the continuous-batcher is forming many smaller batches and more requests are hitting the small-seq fallback. perf-bot posted a summary: <https://perf.internal/runs/1882|run/1882>

perf-bot: perf-summary: canary 13B p3.2x: throughput -12% (tokens/sec), p50 latency +8ms. Flamegraph + traces here: https://perf.internal/flame/1882. Top two hotspots: kernel-selection overhead & extra kernel launches for seq<64.

marta: Which config was active for the batcher on that canary? paged_kv enabled? any prefetching?

josh: This was the canary that also included PR#5423 (kernel selector tweak). It lowered the min_tokens_for_flash threshold from 128 -> 64. Commit: 7a3f2be. paged_kv prefetch=true in runtime config.

priya: Quick profiling numbers from a small microbench (single-GPU):
```
seq  tokens  FlashAttention(ms)  HybridKernel(ms)
32   512     2.9                 1.8
64   1024    3.6                 2.9
128  2048    4.6                 4.2
256  4096    6.8                 7.4
```
FlashAttention shows higher per-request latency at seq=32/64 vs hybrid for small sequences. Combined with lower threshold, we now route many small seqs into a slower path due to launch overhead + inability to coalesce tokens in time.

alex: That matches what I saw — batcher is trying to keep p99 latency low so it flushes earlier, ending up with small batches. Two quick levers we could try: bump continuous-batcher token_budget_target for the offending queue from 4096 -> 8192 OR increase sample_window_ms so coalescing waits slightly longer. Both are low-risk canary configs.

sara: Another idea: change the queue sampler to prioritize predicted total_tokens rather than request_count. Currently we pick N requests up to token_budget; if we bias by estimated_total_tokens (head_seq + remaining), we avoid many small-seq flushes. Pseudocode: `score = remaining_tokens + alpha * head_len` then sort.

marta: Good call. Can we test both iterator-level sampler change and token_budget bump as two separate canaries? josh can you run those?

josh: Will do. Plan:
- Canary A: token_budget_target=8192 for the 13B queue, keep current sampler
- Canary B: sampler_by_estimated_tokens (alpha=0.5), token_budget_target=4096
Command I'll run: `tools/deploy_canary --pool=13b-canary --config=canaryA.json` and `... --config=canaryB.json`

deploy-bot: Canary deployments started: canaryA=deployed at 1882345720, canaryB=deployed at 1882345745.

perf-bot: Preliminary metrics (+2m):
- canaryA: throughput +6%, p50 -3ms, p99 unchanged
- canaryB: throughput +9%, p50 -6ms, p99 -1ms
Link: https://perf.internal/canary/1882/summary

alex: Nice. sampler_by_estimated_tokens looks promising. But we still have a residual memcpy hotspot when paged_kv prefetch is enabled. priya can you share the trace?

priya: Trace snippet: `cudaMemcpyAsync (paged_kv_prefetch) -> 18% GPU wall time` and in the callstack we see repeated prefetches for KV pages that are immediately evicted by the batch. Suspect we are prefetching at request arrival rather than at batch-formation time.

marta: So ordering issue: we prefetch per-request before coalescing; need to move prefetch to after token coalesce and before kernel launch. That would reduce wasted copies. Could also add a prefetch budget cap per-batch.

josh: Quick patch: move paged_kv.prefetch() into batcher.prepare_batch() and add `prefetch_max_bytes=8MB` config. I'll push a small canary.

deploy-bot: Patch branch `fix/prefetch-after-coalesce` deployed as canaryC at 1882345810.

perf-bot: CanaryC metrics (+3m): throughput +11%, cuda memcpy time down to 6% of GPU wall time. Full traces: https://perf.internal/trace/1882/canaryC

alex: Great win. Action items:
- josh: merge sampler_by_estimated_tokens after adding unit tests for score function (owner: josh)
- josh: merge prefetch-after-coalesce + add `prefetch_max_bytes` feature flag (owner: josh)
- priya: run extended perf run 24h with canaryC to validate tail stability (owner: priya)
- marta: update rollout plan (owner: marta)

priya: Filed follow-up ticket: INF-2417 (24h perf run + regression guards).

alex: Thanks everyone. Adding :eyes: reaction. We'll reconvene if any regression shows up in the extended run.
